lines: One chunk holds at least 90.0 % of a page, so the browser fetches practically the whole page before it shows anything:
launchpad-main.js: 1 file, 9,544,472 B, and 8 chunks of 547,792 B its runtime loads later, of which launchpad-main.js is 9,544,472 B (94.6 %).
launchpad-admin.js: 1 file, 8,469,348 B, and 8 chunks of 547,792 B its runtime loads later, of which launchpad-admin.js is 8,469,348 B (93.9 %).

Code splitting puts what the first paint does not need behind a dynamic import, and then the browser fetches it when the code asks. Which part of a page that is does not follow from the build output; the source decides it.
2 packages are imported by their root in src, so the whole barrel is reachable and the bundler keeps whatever it cannot prove unused:

@nextcloud/vue: 1,830,237 B in 266 modules, 19.2 % of the static path of launchpad-main.js, imported by its root in 10 files: components/DashboardConfigMenu.vue (NcActionButton, NcActions), components/DashboardConfigModal.vue (NcButton, NcCheckboxRadioSwitch, NcModal, ...), and 8 more. It is imported per module as well, through 6 other specifiers.

gridstack: 93,472 B in 14 modules, 1.0 % of the static path of launchpad-main.js, imported by its root in components/DashboardGrid.vue (GridStack) and components/Widgets/Renderers/ContainerWidget.vue. It is imported per module as well, through 1 other specifier.
Importing the module that is used instead of the package root lets the bundler drop the rest of the barrel.
ncmake's lint-vue-imports workflow gates exactly this specifier for @nextcloud/vue, so this finding is that red check with a byte figure attached.

10 delivered files look like a webpack or CommonJS bundle. Their internal structure is not derivable from the artefact, so each counts as one file and the chunk figures below say nothing about what is inside them.
Every delivered file in js carries a source map, so every byte can be charged to the package and the module it came from.
